records.statement: For any two orders of n labels, the sharp universal guaranteed nonadjacent-in-both-orders subset size is ceil(n/4).
records.justification: Self-contained lower and sharp upper bound argument archived in sessions/S002/MATHEMATICS.md; academic source establishes overlapping braid-graph subject, not the exact formula.
records.limitations: Human proof only; no Lean formalisation, independent referee or novel status; classical argument.

records.statement: OEIS A343447 concerns alternating 101...101 multiples for every positive integer coprime to 10.
records.justification: Inspected OEIS entry directly.
records.limitations: The statement is known, not an S002 discovery.

records.statement: After any two opposite-colour cells are deleted from an even-by-even rectangular board, the rest is domino-tileable.
records.justification: Inspected opposite-colour removal proof and named theorem secondary entry; Hamiltonian cycle gives even paths.
records.limitations: Source primary attribution to Gomory not independently checked.

records.statement: Every n>=1 with gcd(n,10)=1 divides a decimal palindrome with one central 2 and all other digits 1.
records.justification: Use P_k=((10^(k+1)-1)(10^k+1))/9, k=ord_(9n)(10)-1, so the first factor is a multiple of 9n.
records.limitations: Elementary human modular-order proof; no machine formalisation and no novel research result asserted.

records.statement: A hole-free checkerboard-balanced polyomino need not admit a domino tiling.
records.justification: Explicit eight-cell comb-like polyomino has equal colours and two leaves with one common neighbour, giving Hall violation.
records.limitations: Concrete symbolic counterexample, not computational enumeration.

records.statement: For any three permutations of [n], sharp largest-set worst-case nonconsecutivity equals ceil(n/6).
records.justification: 5-degenerate union of three paths yields 6-colouring; three explicit edge-disjoint Hamilton paths decompose K6, and concatenated small clique blocks attain the upper bound.
records.limitations: Symbolic elementary proof only; SRC-0006 addresses a related two-path graph class, not this exact statement or originality.

records.statement: The fixed-label strengthening of ceil(n/4) for two permutations fails at n=5.
records.justification: Orders a,v,b,c,d and c,v,d,a,b make v adjacent to all other four labels.
records.limitations: Exact five-vertex explicit counterexample; no general strengthening investigated.

records.statement: CND-0050 has the exact identity s(n)=A039836(2n)+1 and is a restatement of known weak Sidon set extremality.
records.justification: Pair sums collide only for disjoint pairs when the two unordered pairs differ; hence no four distinct equal-sum elements is precisely weak Sidon. OEIS A039836 directly names the same maximum over [1,N].
records.limitations: No claim that general terms/closed-form maximum are known; related 2026 arXiv result concerns a different weak-Sidon question.

records.statement: For every finite connected simple triangle-free graph G with minimum degree at least 2, are there two cycles sharing no edge? — DISPOSITION: The 5-cycle C5 is triangle-free, connected and 2-regular, yet has only one cycle.
records.justification: The 5-cycle C5 is triangle-free, connected and 2-regular, yet has only one cycle. Minimum degree cannot force two cycles: C5 has only five edges; a graph-theoretic cyclomatic-number check is 1. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: In every finite connected undirected graph all of whose vertices have even degree, does each edge lie on a simple cycle? — DISPOSITION: A bridge would create a component with odd total degree (its one exiting edge); hence no bridge exists. Any nonbridge edge lies on a cycle.
records.justification: A bridge would create a component with odd total degree (its one exiting edge); hence no bridge exists. Any nonbridge edge lies on a cycle. Bridge parity is sufficient: remove edge uv, find a remaining u-v path, reattach edge to form a cycle. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: Does every finite connected graph having precisely two vertices of odd degree admit a trail traversing every edge exactly once? — DISPOSITION: Add an edge between the two odd-degree vertices to get all-even degrees; Euler circuit exists and removing added edge gives the required trail.
records.justification: Add an edge between the two odd-degree vertices to get all-even degrees; Euler circuit exists and removing added edge gives the required trail. Euler's trail theorem directly settles all quantifiers; nontree multigraph insertion is allowed in the proof auxiliary graph. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Source grade given in SOURCES; only statement inspected as recorded, independent full theorem proof not claimed.

records.statement: In normal play on a pile of n positive stones with moves remove 1 or 2 stones, does the first player win exactly when 3 does not divide n? — DISPOSITION: Positions divisible by 3 are losing: any move leaves remainder 1 or 2, and the opponent can restore a multiple of 3; all other positions move to such a multiple.
records.justification: Positions divisible by 3 are losing: any move leaves remainder 1 or 2, and the opponent can restore a multiple of 3; all other positions move to such a multiple. Induction on n, with terminal zero losing for the player to move. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: For every finite multiset of positive integers of even total sum, can repeated replacement of any two numbers a,b by |a-b| finish at 0? — DISPOSITION: For {1,2,5}, the possible first differences give final values 4 (merge 1,2), 2 (merge 1,5), or 2 (merge 2,5), never 0.
records.justification: For {1,2,5}, the possible first differences give final values 4 (merge 1,2), 2 (merge 1,5), or 2 (merge 2,5), never 0. Parity is invariant but insufficient; this explicit three-number exhaustive symbolic split disproves sufficiency. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: For every finite binary word, is the irreducible word obtained by repeatedly deleting 00 or 11 independent of the chosen sequence of deletions? — DISPOSITION: Termination is by decreasing length by 2. Two redexes either are disjoint and commute or overlap in 000/111 and both choices leave the same letter; induction on remaining length gives unique irreducible normal form.
records.justification: Termination is by decreasing length by 2. Two redexes either are disjoint and commute or overlap in 000/111 and both choices leave the same letter; induction on remaining length gives unique irreducible normal form. Local diamond plus length induction, not brute-force enumeration or an unsupported confluence citation. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: In every infinite binary word, for every k>=1 do two adjacent blocks of the same length at least k occur with equal counts of 1? — DISPOSITION: Exactly the classical arbitrarily long abelian-square theorem of Entringer, Jackson and Schatz (1974); direct authors' paper statement inspected in a public text reproduction.
records.justification: Exactly the classical arbitrarily long abelian-square theorem of Entringer, Jackson and Schatz (1974); direct authors' paper statement inspected in a public text reproduction. For binary words two equal-length blocks have the same ones count iff they have equal multisets of letters; identity is bidirectional. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Source grade given in SOURCES; only statement inspected as recorded, independent full theorem proof not claimed.

records.statement: Does every infinite binary word contain three consecutive blocks of some common length at least 2 with equal numbers of 1? — DISPOSITION: Rao and Rosenfeld (2015) state that no infinite binary word avoids abelian cubes of period >=2; binary Parikh equality equals equality of ones counts.
records.justification: Rao and Rosenfeld (2015) state that no infinite binary word avoids abelian cubes of period >=2; binary Parikh equality equals equality of ones counts. Do not mistake 'period >=2' for 'arbitrarily large period': these are different quantifier statements. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Source grade given in SOURCES; only statement inspected as recorded, independent full theorem proof not claimed.

records.statement: For all m,n>=2 and all binary m-by-n boards, can flipping all four bits of chosen adjacent 2-by-2 subboards reach all zeroes iff every initial row sum and column sum is even? — DISPOSITION: Each move preserves each row and column parity. Conversely clear positions (i,j), i<m,j<n, lexicographically using a flip based at (i,j) iff its bit is 1; the last row and column vanish by the parity constraints.
records.justification: Each move preserves each row and column parity. Conversely clear positions (i,j), i<m,j<n, lexicographically using a flip based at (i,j) iff its bit is 1; the last row and column vanish by the parity constraints. Constructive elimination works for arbitrary m,n >=2; earlier cleared cells never change. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: For every m,n>=2, is a binary m-by-n grid with even total bit sum necessarily transformable to zero by adjacent 2-by-2 flips? — DISPOSITION: The 2-by-2 board with top row 11 and bottom row 00 has even total 2 but each column has odd parity, preserved by every allowed flip.
records.justification: The 2-by-2 board with top row 11 and bottom row 00 has even total 2 but each column has odd parity, preserved by every allowed flip. Checks row/column invariants from CND-0059 rather than number of black cells alone. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: For every n>=1 does {1,...,2n} have a partition into n unordered pairs {a,b} with a+b prime? — DISPOSITION: Greenfield and Greenfield (1998) established this; standard Bertrand-postulate induction explicitly inspected in secondary exposition; OEIS A000341 enumerates such pairings.
records.justification: Greenfield and Greenfield (1998) established this; standard Bertrand-postulate induction explicitly inspected in secondary exposition; OEIS A000341 enumerates such pairings. For n>=2 choose prime p with 2n<p<4n and pair the consecutive upper suffix [p-2n,2n] by equal-sum nested pairs, then induct on remaining prefix. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Source grade given in SOURCES; only statement inspected as recorded, independent full theorem proof not claimed.

records.statement: For every n>=1 can {1,...,2n} be partitioned into n pairs whose sums are n pairwise distinct primes? — DISPOSITION: Already directly posed and answered on Math.SE in 2018; n=7 impossible because sum 1+...+14=105, whereas the seven largest distinct eligible odd primes <=27 total only 95.
records.justification: Already directly posed and answered on Math.SE in 2018; n=7 impossible because sum 1+...+14=105, whereas the seven largest distinct eligible odd primes <=27 total only 95. Each pair uses two distinct positive integers and prime sum is odd <=4n-1; a rainbow matching would need distinct prime labels, contradicted by total-sum ceiling. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: For all n>=1, given n red and n blue distinct planar points with no three collinear, does a noncrossing perfect matching using straight red-blue segments exist? — DISPOSITION: Known geometric matching theorem (Kano 2002 presentation). Independent short proof: choose a red-blue perfect matching minimizing total Euclidean length; any crossing edges can be uncrossed by swapping blue endpoints to strictly reduce length.
records.justification: Known geometric matching theorem (Kano 2002 presentation). Independent short proof: choose a red-blue perfect matching minimizing total Euclidean length; any crossing edges can be uncrossed by swapping blue endpoints to strictly reduce length. Uncrossing uses the triangle inequality with strictness from general position; minimizer therefore has no crossing. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Source grade given in SOURCES; only statement inspected as recorded, independent full theorem proof not claimed.

records.statement: For every n>=1, place 1,...,2n clockwise around a convex circle. Does a perfect noncrossing straight-chord matching exist in which endpoints of every chord sum to a prime? — DISPOSITION: Bertrand induction picks p in (2n,4n) and pairs a=p-2n with 2n, a+1 with 2n-1, etc. These chords are nested and do not cross; induct on the disjoint smaller prefix [1,a-1].
records.justification: Bertrand induction picks p in (2n,4n) and pairs a=p-2n with 2n, a+1 with 2n-1, etc. These chords are nested and do not cross; induct on the disjoint smaller prefix [1,a-1]. This is already implicit in known 'intervallic' prime pairings discussed on MathOverflow in 2016, not a novel open problem. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.

records.statement: For every finite tree T on n>=2 vertices, is there a bijection f:V(T)->{1,...,n} for which f(u)+f(v) is prime on every edge uv? — DISPOSITION: The five-vertex star K1,4 refutes it: any centre label c in {1,2,3,4,5} forces four prime sums with other labels, but c=1,2,3,4,5 respectively gives composite sums 4,6,4,6,6.
records.justification: The five-vertex star K1,4 refutes it: any centre label c in {1,2,3,4,5} forces four prime sums with other labels, but c=1,2,3,4,5 respectively gives composite sums 4,6,4,6,6. A single composite edge for each of five possible central labels suffices; no computation run. Full reasoning in sessions/S004/MATHEMATICS.md.
records.limitations: Elementary argument/witness internal, not separately peer-refereed or formally verified; not novel.
